title: Construction of AC/DC magnetic syringe device for stimulated drug release, injection and ejection of nanocarriers and testing cytotoxicity in vitro
author: Zjalić, Mustapić, et al.

steps.title: Fabricate permalloy syringe body and piston
steps.instruction: Turn a 150 mm long, 5–8 mm diameter permalloy rod on a lathe to produce a syringe body 100 mm long, inner diameter 3.25 mm, outer diameter 6.00 mm, with a Luer‑type tip (outer diameter 3.924–4.026 mm, inner diameter 2 mm). Turn a medical‑grade PTFE piston to a final diameter of 3.24 mm. Keep tolerances for body and piston within ±0.005 mm.

steps.title: Prepare Luer‑type permalloy needle and sterilize
steps.instruction: Order a permalloy needle with a Luer‑type metal hub, length 35 mm and G26 thickness. Sterilize the needle at 121 °C for 20 min before use.

steps.title: Wind 23 AWG coil onto syringe
steps.instruction: Cut ~4 m of 23 AWG varnish‑insulated copper wire. Mark a 6.5 cm section on the syringe body for the coil. Measure 15 cm of wire, bend it 90°, and place the bend at one end of the marked region (the short segment will become the coil terminal). Wind the remaining wire tightly around the marked length to give 1000 turns in 9 layers (≈112 winds per layer) with no spacing. After each layer, fix the wire temporarily with a piece of Kapton tape. After the final layer, leave a 15 cm terminal length, cover the whole coil with two layers of Kapton tape, and slide the coil off the mould. Burn off 2 cm of insulation from each terminal, solder silicone‑insulated leads, and attach safety‑type banana jacks.

steps.title: Assemble coil, needle, and connect to power supply
steps.instruction: Slide the finished coil onto the syringe body, fit the permalloy needle onto the Luer tip, and connect the coil terminals to a laboratory variable voltage/current/frequency power supply using the banana jacks.

steps.title: Test and fix coil position
steps.instruction: Pass current through the coil and verify needle magnetization. Move the coil up and down the syringe body until maximal inductance is observed, then fix the coil in place with fast‑curing epoxy resin applying two dot‑like drops on each side of the coil.

steps.title: Sterilize assembled magnetic syringe
steps.instruction: Autoclave the assembled syringe (with coil) at 105 °C for 20 min, then dry in a laboratory oven at 50 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Synthesize magnetic nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Prepare a detergent solution by dissolving 1.5 g CTAB and 1.5 g SDS in 30 ml deionized water, then add 60 ml cyclohexane and stir until clear. Degas the solution under N₂ by bubbling nitrogen through it. Assemble a gas‑purging setup by drilling two holes in a rubber stopper, inserting two 4 mm tubes (one long, immersed in the solution; one short, bent 180° outward), and mounting the stopper on a round‑bottom flask. While degassing, prepare 20 ml of 0.0015 M FeCl₂ solution and 20 ml of 0.003 M FeCl₃ solution in Type 1 water (FeCl₂ under inert gas, FeCl₃ open to air). Stir both solutions for 30 min. In an inert atmosphere, mix the two iron solutions in a separate flask and add 5 ml of 30 % ammonia dropwise over 1 min. After 1 min, add the detergent solution and vortex gently. After 5 min, collect the formed nanoparticles with an external permanent magnet, wash repeatedly first with Type 1 water then with acetone (centrifuge ≥5 min at 10 000 g if needed), dry overnight at 60 °C, then heat at 250 °C for 2 h under inert atmosphere to remove residual detergent.

steps.title: Adsorb methylene blue onto nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Prepare 20 ml of 0.001 M methylene blue (MB) in Type 1 water in a flask with a ground‑glass neck. Weigh 100 mg of the dried Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles and add them to the MB solution. Degas the suspension at 1 × 10³ Pa for 1 h at +4 °C while bubbling nitrogen (or another inert gas) to remove dissolved oxygen. Cap the flask, wrap the neck and cap with laboratory paraffin film, and leave the suspension overnight at room temperature to allow MB adsorption.

steps.title: Wash and freeze‑dry MB‑loaded nanoparticles
steps.instruction: The next day, collect the MB‑loaded nanoparticles with a rare‑earth magnet, wash them four times with 50 ml Type 1 water for 10 min each (until the wash water runs clear), then freeze‑dry them. If a freeze‑dryer is unavailable, place the nanoparticles at the bottom of a 50 ml Falcon tube containing 50 g anhydrous calcium sulfate or silica gel, add a 1 cm thick wad of cotton wool, insert an open Eppendorf tube into the cotton, seal the Falcon tube, and freeze at –80 °C for 7 days before thawing to obtain dry particles.

steps.title: Set up magnetic release platform
steps.instruction: In a 30 ml beaker, disperse the MB‑treated nanoparticles in water and split the suspension into three equal 25 ml beakers. Build a 2.5 cm‑high platform by stacking three laboratory plastic bottle caps. Between the caps, place two stacks of permanent rare‑earth magnets (each stack: five 12 mm‑diameter button magnets) spaced 5 cm apart. Immerse the prepared magnetic needle in the nanoparticle suspension, clamp the whole assembly firmly to a laboratory stand with aluminium clamps.

steps.title: Perform AC/DC stimulation and collect samples
steps.instruction: Set the power supply to a current of 100 mA and select a frequency between 1 Hz and 15 Hz. For each frequency, use a different aliquot of nanoparticle suspension. After stimulation, withdraw 1 ml of suspension, transfer it to a 1 ml cuvette and measure the optical density at 580 nm. Simultaneously add an equal volume of Type 1 water to a separate beaker containing the same suspension to keep the total volume constant.

steps.title: Sample according to release schedule
steps.instruction: Collect a sample every 10 min for the first hour and one additional sample after two hours of needle immersion.

steps.title: Clean and sterilize glass coverslips
steps.instruction: Mix 1 part 30 % H₂O₂ with 9 parts concentrated (96 %) H₂SO₄ (e.g., 10 ml H₂O₂ + 90 ml H₂SO₄) in a 300 ml wide‑throat Duran or Pyrex Erlenmeyer flask under a fume hood, wearing nitrile gloves. Swirl gently for 10 min, then place 100 coverslips (15 × 15 mm squares or 12 mm circles) into a second 300 ml flask and add the acid mixture, swirling to cover all coverslips. Repeat the swirl at least three times over the next 30 min (watch glass or petri dish cover recommended). After 30 min, pour the acid into a 5 L bucket of distilled water, then add 200 ml distilled water to the coverslip flask, swirl and discard. Rinse the coverslips by adding 200 ml distilled water and placing the flask on an orbital shaker at 100 rpm for 1 h; repeat this wash cycle five more times (total 6 h). After the final wash, discard the water, add 100 ml ACS/HPLC‑grade methanol, swirl for 5 min and discard. Cover the flask opening with aluminium foil and dry‑sterilize the coverslips in an oven at 270 °C for 5 h.

steps.title: Prepare iron nanoparticle stock solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 mg of iron nanoparticles (INP) and place them in a sterile 2 ml Eppendorf tube. Add 1 ml cell‑growth medium (without FBS) to obtain a 10 mg ml⁻¹ stock. Vortex at maximum speed for 30 s until no clumps remain.

steps.title: Make working nanoparticle dilutions
steps.instruction: Calculate the required volumes for each desired concentration, taking the stock volume into account. Before pipetting, mix the stock by aspirating and dispensing 10 times. Dilute the stock in appropriately sized Falcon tubes, and before transferring each working solution to a well, mix it by pipetting up and down 4 times.

steps.title: Seed cells on collagen‑coated coverslips and treat
steps.instruction: Wash the acid‑cleaned coverslips and coat them with collagen as described earlier. Seed the chosen cell line (e.g., differentiated SY‑SY5Y) at the prescribed density, differentiate for 9 days, then treat with the prepared INP solutions. After treatment, remove the growth medium and add 500 µl of 2 % buffered paraformaldehyde (PFA). Incubate at +4 °C for 30 min, then wash five times with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Perform Prussian blue staining
steps.instruction: Prepare 25 ml of 2 % aqueous potassium ferrocyanide and mix with 25 ml of 4 % hydrochloric acid; filter the mixture through filter paper. Remove PBS from the wells and add 500 µl of the freshly prepared solution to each well; incubate at room temperature for 30 min. Rinse the wells six times with distilled water, then stain with Nuclear Fast Red counterstain, rinsing until the wash is clear. Dehydrate the cells in absolute ethanol, clear in xylene, mount with resinous mounting medium, and cover with a coverslip. Positive reaction appears as blue staining within cells.

steps.title: Prepare MTT stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve MTT to make a stock solution (concentration not specified) and store at –20 °C; the stock is stable for at least 6 months.

steps.title: Conduct MTT cytotoxicity assay
steps.instruction: Seed cells in collagen‑coated 24‑well plates (minimum six biological replicates per concentration and control). Replace the growth medium with medium containing the appropriate INP concentration and incubate for 24 h. Add 50 µl of MTT stock to each well (final tetrazolium bromide concentration 0.5 mg ml⁻¹). Gently swirl and incubate for 4 h at 37 °C to allow formazan crystal formation. Add 500 µl of MTT solvent to each well and pipette up and down 10 times to dissolve the crystals. Transfer the entire well content to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 15 000 g for 5 min at room temperature to pellet nanoparticles. Pipette 200 µl of the supernatant into individual wells of a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate and read absorbance at 595 nm. Calculate the percentage viability relative to the untreated control. (If using a 48‑ or 96‑well plate, adjust volumes accordingly, e.g., 200 µl total per well and transfer 100 µl supernatant after centrifugation.)

description: Construction of AC/DC magnetic syringe device for stimulated drug release, injection and ejection of magnetic nanoparticles
